    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
),
customer_totals AS (
    SELECT c.customer_unique_id,
           MAX(o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS latest_purchase,
           COUNT(*) AS total_orders,
           CASE WHEN COUNT(p.spend) = COUNT(*)
                THEN ROUND(SUM(p.spend), 2)
           END AS total_spend
    FROM orders AS o
    JOIN customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    LEFT JOIN order_spend AS p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
    GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id
),
recency AS (
    -- Elapsed days from each customer's last delivered purchase to the
    -- latest delivered purchase in the dataset, retaining time of day.
    SELECT t.*,
           JULIANDAY(MAX(latest_purchase) OVER ()) - JULIANDAY(latest_purchase) AS recency_days
    FROM customer_totals AS t
),
percentiles AS (
    -- Best first: shorter recency, more orders, and higher spend.
    -- Equal values share a percentile. Unknown spend is not scored for M.
    SELECT r.*,
           CUME_DIST() OVER (ORDER BY recency_days) AS r_pct,
           CUME_DIST() OVER (ORDER BY total_orders DESC) AS f_pct,
           CASE WHEN total_spend IS NOT NULL THEN
               CUME_DIST() OVER (PARTITION BY (total_spend IS NULL) ORDER BY total_spend DESC)
           END AS m_pct
    FROM recency AS r
),
scores AS (
    -- Scores 1 to 5 use cumulative cutoffs of 20%, 40%, 60%, and 80%, inclusive.
    SELECT customer_unique_id, total_orders, total_spend,
           1 + (r_pct > 0.2) + (r_pct > 0.4) + (r_pct > 0.6) + (r_pct > 0.8) AS r_score,
           1 + (f_pct > 0.2) + (f_pct > 0.4) + (f_pct > 0.6) + (f_pct > 0.8) AS f_score,
           1 + (m_pct > 0.2) + (m_pct > 0.4) + (m_pct > 0.6) + (m_pct > 0.8) AS m_score
    FROM percentiles
),
segment_inputs AS (
    SELECT customer_unique_id, total_orders, total_spend, r_score, f_score + m_score AS fm_score
    FROM scores
),
segmented AS (
    SELECT customer_unique_id, total_orders, total_spend,
           CASE
               WHEN r_score = 1 AND fm_score BETWEEN 1 AND 4 THEN 'Champions'
               WHEN r_score IN (4, 5) AND fm_score BETWEEN 1 AND 2 THEN 'Can''t Lose Them'
               WHEN r_score IN (4, 5) AND fm_score BETWEEN 3 AND 6 THEN 'Hibernating'
               WHEN r_score IN (4, 5) AND fm_score BETWEEN 7 AND 10 THEN 'Lost'
               WHEN r_score IN (2, 3) AND fm_score BETWEEN 1 AND 4 THEN 'Loyal Customers'
               WHEN r_score = 3 AND fm_score BETWEEN 5 AND 6 THEN 'Needs Attention'
               WHEN r_score = 1 AND fm_score BETWEEN 7 AND 8 THEN 'Recent Users'
               WHEN (r_score = 1 AND fm_score BETWEEN 5 AND 6)

               WHEN r_score = 1 AND fm_score BETWEEN 9 AND 10 THEN 'Price Sensitive'
               WHEN r_score = 2 AND fm_score BETWEEN 9 AND 10 THEN 'Promising'
               WHEN r_score = 3 AND fm_score BETWEEN 7 AND 10 THEN 'About to Sleep'
           END AS rfm_segment
    FROM segment_inputs

FROM segmented

    SELECT b.striker AS player_id,
           b.match_id,
           SUM(s.runs_scored) AS match_runs
    FROM ball_by_ball AS b
    JOIN batsman_scored AS s
      ON s.match_id = b.match_id
     AND s.innings_no = b.innings_no
     AND s.over_id = b.over_id
     AND s.ball_id = b.ball_id
    GROUP BY b.striker, b.match_id
),
played_matches AS (
    SELECT player_id, match_id
    FROM player_match
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.player_id, r.match_id
    FROM runs_by_player_match AS r
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM player_match AS pm
        WHERE pm.player_id = r.player_id
          AND pm.match_id = r.match_id
    )
),
player_averages AS (
    SELECT pm.player_id,
           AVG(COALESCE(r.match_runs, 0)) AS avg_runs_per_match

    GROUP BY pm.player_id
)
